newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana president's widow becomes prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Guyana president's widow becomes prime minister.

text.p: Janet Jagan, widow of former Guyanese President Cheddi Jagan, was sworn in on Monday as Guyana's first female prime minister and said public support following her husband's death had convinced her to take the job.
Jagan, 76, was also appointed first vice-president and is expected to lead her husband's People's Progressive Party (PPP) in presidential elections later this year, party sources said.
The appointment of Jagan, the first foreign-born prime minister, came just over a week after Cheddi Jagan died of heart failure at the Walter Reed hospital in Washington. He was 78.
More than one in four of the 800,000 population of this former British colony came to view Jagan's body lie in state before last Thursday's cremation.
Jagan's son Cheddi Jagan Jr cast his father's ashes into Guyana's three main rivers -- the Ezequibo, Demerara and Berbice -- from a helicopter on Monday.
Wearing a black dress of mourning, Jagan was sworn in at a simple ceremony at the presidential secretariat's office in central Georgetown.

"It never entered my mind to that I'd be prime minister or anything," Jagan told Reuters after the ceremony. "But then I saw all these other people and they connected me so clearly to Cheddi and everyone told me that I had to carry on, had to take the responsibility."
A U.S.-trained nurse Jagan came to the South American country, then British Guiana, in 1943 and has been extensively involved in the country's politics.

As first deputy speaker of the House of Assembly she held several ministerial posts in PPP governments under British rule and was imprisoned for six months following the suspension of the Constitution and ouster of the government in 1955. She is still a member of parliament.
President Samuel Hinds, the former prime minister sworn in to lead the country following Jagan's death, said he made the appointment after consultation with cabinet colleagues and PPP leaders.
